report:
Gitea Action fails to upload to its own LFS

### Description

I am trying to compile a rather large file automatically inside a workflow/action. The compilation works fine, however when it becomes time to push the ISO with LFS to Gitea from the action runner. It fails with:
```
2025/08/21 09:37:47 .../lfs/content_store.go:58:(*ContentStore).Put() [E] Whilst putting LFS OID[2d285650884475f20a98ae505d113ab64cdd0e864b90c6ef230d5be57c8f663a]: Failed to copy to tmpPath: 2d/28/5650884475f20a98ae505d113ab64cdd0e864b90c6ef230d5be57c8f663a Error: unexpected EOF
2025/08/21 09:37:47 services/lfs/server.go:333:UploadHandler.1() [E] Error putting LFS MetaObject [2d285650884475f20a98ae505d113ab64cdd0e864b90c6ef230d5be57c8f663a] into content store. Error: unexpected EOF
2025/08/21 09:37:47 services/lfs/server.go:346:UploadHandler() [E] Error whilst uploadOrVerify LFS OID[2d285650884475f20a98ae505d113ab64cdd0e864b90c6ef230d5be57c8f663a]: unexpected EOF
2025/08/21 09:37:47 HTTPRequest [I] router: completed PUT /daanselen/ntos.git/info/lfs/objects/2d285650884475f20a98ae505d113ab64cdd0e864b90c6ef230d5be57c8f663a/989855744 for 10.222.222.240:41932, 500 Internal Server Error in 60020.4ms @ lfs/server.go:280(lfs.UploadHandler)
```
The 'client' git push is:
```
09:39:54.684587 trace git-lfs: tq: starting transfer adapter "basic"
09:39:54.684844 trace git-lfs: HTTP: PUT https://mygiteadomain/daanselen/ntos.git/info/lfs/objects/{objectid}/{somenumbers}
09:40:54.764998 trace git-lfs: HTTP: 502
09:40:54.765150 trace git-lfs: tq: retrying object {objectid}: Fatal error: Server error https://mygiteadomain/daanselen/ntos.git/info/lfs/objects/{objectid}/{somenumbers}from HTTP 502
```

Any Idea how to fix this or how to handle this?

The ingress is done through a route:
```
annotations:
        traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/client-max-body-size: 10GB
        traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "600"
        traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-send-timeout: "600"
```

```
config:
<SNAP>
    http:
      postBuffer: 624288000
    server:
      LFS_START_SERVER: true
      MAX_LFS_FILE_SIZE: 5GB
<SNAP>
    lfs:
      PATH: /lfs
      concurrenttransfers: 10
      activitytimeout: 3600
      dialtimeout: 3600
      keepalive: 3600
      tlstimeout: 3600
    actions:
      ENABLED: true
```

IMPORTANT! Manually pushing works just fine with LFS. So its something inside Gitea/workflow.

```
      - name: Upload the recompiled ISO to the custom-iso branch
        run: |
          cd ${{ env.WORKPLACE }}

          git config user.name "Gitea CI/CD"
          git config user.email "servicedesk@domain.com"
          git lfs install --local
          git config lfs.https://mygiteadomain/daanselen/ntos.git/info/lfs.locksverify true
          git checkout -B custom-iso

          mv ${{ env.WORKPLACE }}/iso/debian-${{ env.DEBIAN_VERSION }}-amd64-autoinstall.iso ./debian-${{ env.DEBIAN_VERSION }}-amd64-autoinstall.iso
          git add ./debian-${{ env.DEBIAN_VERSION }}-amd64-autoinstall.iso
          git commit -m "Update custom ISO: $(date +'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')" || echo "No changes to commit"

          git push -u https://${{ secrets.GITEA_USER }}:${{ secrets.GITEA_TOKEN }}@mygiteadomain/daanselen/ntos.git custom-iso --force
```

### Gitea Version

1.24.5

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Gitea demo site?

No

### Log Gist

The above are the relevant logs.

### Git Version

Whatever is installer on the action-runner with ubuntu-latest (varies)

### Operating System

Debian Kubernetes

### How are you running Gitea?

Helm charts. for both Gitea and the Actions

### Database

PostgreSQL

evidence.quote: `60020.4ms` `HTTP: 502` Clearly it is caused by your reverse proxy. There is a 60s timeout

confirmation.quote: You do seem to know what you are doing. Making the timeout half an hour makes it work. Thank you.

notes: Traefik reverse-proxy 60s timeout cut the LFS upload (Gitea logged the cancelled body read as unexpected EOF); fixed purely by raising the proxy timeout, no Gitea change (timeline has no cross-refs). Not an upgrade regression.

reviews.decidable_why: The body contains the 60020 ms duration, the client's 502 after 60 s and the Traefik ingress config, which together point to a proxy timeout.
Body logs show exactly ~60s duration plus 502 from a Traefik ingress, a classic proxy timeout signature.
